transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-18
Start: 16:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Lena (Orion Head of ML), Ravi (Platform Eng), Julie (PM), Tom (Data Eng)
---
00:00 Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh quick agenda — align on eval playbook, confirm success criteria and the shortlist, and agree timeline.
00:18 Lena (Orion): Thanks, Maya. Quick context — Orion's main use case is automated extraction and summarization from legal and financial filings. We need high precision on certain fields; can't have hallucinations on monetary terms.
00:33 Ethan (Redwood): Got it. Quick Q on scale — what is your steady-state RPS and peak?
00:39 Ravi (Orion): Steady is low today, maybe 5 rps, but target for production is 30–50 rps p95. Batch jobs will also run nightly — think many docs but latency less important there.
00:52 Maya (Redwood): And any hard latency SLOs?
00:55 Julie (Orion): For API calls in interactive mode, we want p95 under 250 ms ideally, but we can stretch to 400ms if quality is materially better. Cost target — roughly to keep inference cost below $1 per 1k processed docs on average, but that's a soft target.
01:12 Ethan (Redwood): For the POC we should measure p50/p95, tokens per request, and cost per 1M tokens as a baseline. Also quality: extraction F1, hallucination rate on a golden set.
01:27 Tom (Orion): On data — we'll provide a 10k document sample (mix English + German + French). Most are English, ~15% German, ~5% French. Schema is multi-lingual legal/financial forms.
01:45 Maya (Redwood): Good. Proposed shortlist for the open-model sweep: Llama-3-8B-instruct, Mistral-Instruct-7B-v0.2, OpenLLaMA-13B-tuned, and Falcon-40B-instruct as a heavier test. We can also include a quantized variant where available.
02:05 Lena (Orion): Do we need the 40B for latency reasons? Sounds expensive.
02:09 Ethan (Redwood): The idea is tradeoff coverage — smaller models with LoRA or in-context examples vs bigger model native performance. We'll measure throughput and unit cost; Falcon-40B is to test quality ceiling.
02:25 Ravi (Orion): Important: our infra requires VPC connectivity and SOC2-compliant logging. We'll likely opt for Redwood Dedicated or Private depending on security posture. Can you outline what Dedicated gives us?
02:39 Maya (Redwood): Sure — Dedicated is reserved GPU pools with tenant isolation, private networking options, and audit logs. For Private we can go full VPC and customer-controlled KMS. We'll include both configs in the report.
02:55 Julie (Orion): How about multilingual quality — do models differ much for German legal text?
03:00 Ethan (Redwood): Yes, German and French are hit-or-miss depending on pretraining. We'll baseline with translation + English prompt and compare to native model performance. Also try small domain-tuned LoRA on a labeled subset.
03:18 Lena (Orion): Our main success criteria: extraction F1 > 0.85 on critical fields, hallucination under 5% on golden set, p95 latency < 400ms during 30 rps load, and cost under our soft target.
03:34 Maya (Redwood): Noted. We'll structure the playbook: offline eval (week 1) with automatic metrics, then online latency/capacity tests (week 2), and a short wrap with recommendation + ops runbook (week 3).
03:50 Tom (Orion): For offline eval, do you need labeled data? We can provide ~1k labeled records for critical fields.
03:56 Ethan (Redwood): That's perfect. We'll use that as the golden evaluation set for F1/precision/recall. We'll also run synthetic perturbations to measure hallucination robustness.
04:10 Lena (Orion): Any thoughts on caching and embeddings for retrieval-augmented portions? We do some RAG for long docs.
04:16 Ethan (Redwood): We'll recommend a hybrid: prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts plus a semantic cache for embeddings to avoid repeated encoder cost. Note: test cache hit rates on your workload; it can cut tokens served by 30–60%. Also be aware of tokenization differences across models — affects cache utility.
04:37 Ravi (Orion): Can you run a quick baseline for tokenization differences? Helps us size cost.
04:42 Maya (Redwood): Yes, Ethan will run model tokenization + cost baseline on the provided corpus. We'll push a spreadsheet with per-model token count, p50/p95 latencies, and estimated cost per million tokens.
04:56 Julie (Orion): On rollout strategy, we want canary + automatic fallback to a cheaper variant if latency spikes. Does Redwood support that?
05:02 Maya (Redwood): Yes — Redwood supports routing policies and automatic fallbacks to pinned compatible model variants. We'll include a recommended config in the ops runbook.
05:14 Lena (Orion): Benchmarking cadence — when can we expect first numbers?
05:18 Maya (Redwood): First offline numbers in 5 business days after we get the corpus and labels. End-to-end online tests in 10 business days. Final recommendation and runbook in 3 weeks.
05:30 Tom (Orion): A couple of noisy transcribe notes — sometimes the Fireflies transcript tags speakers generically, sorry if names get swapped.
05:36 Maya (Redwood): No worries, we can reconcile action items in the doc.
05:40 Ethan (Redwood): Quick implementation note — for dedicated benchmarks we'll set up a minimal pool (2 GPUs) to emulate your target throughput, and we can run stress tests to measure p95 at 30–50 rps. We'll also test quantized runs to estimate cost reduction.
05:58 Lena (Orion): Ok that sounds good. We care about reproducibility of results — please include command lines and seed, and note model versions.
06:05 Maya (Redwood): Absolutely. We'll include exact model versions, quantization parameters, and the hardware used.
06:12 Julie (Orion): Final: will Redwood be able to sign an NDA before we upload sample docs?
06:16 Maya (Redwood): Yes, we have a standard NDA and SOC2 paperwork. I'll share the security pack and an NDA link after the call.
06:25 Lena (Orion): Thanks everyone — excited to see the baseline.
06:28 Maya (Redwood): Recap of next steps: Redwood shares eval template and benchmark sheet, Orion uploads corpus + labels, Redwood runs baseline across 4 models and shares results, schedule SE deep dive.
06:40 Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional small speaker attribution errors, some technical terms transcribed (K V cache, intros) imprecisely.
